summary: TechCrunch recaps the rise and collapse of FTX ahead of Sam Bankman-Fried's criminal trial on seven counts of fraud and conspiracy. It traces FTX's founding, its $32 billion valuation, the November 2022 liquidity crisis triggered by Alameda's balance sheet, the bankruptcy, SBF's arrest, and the guilty pleas of Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison. It closes with his legal team and open questions about creditors and tied-up crypto assets.
one_line: A timeline of FTX's rise, November 2022 collapse, and Sam Bankman-Fried's arrest, as his fraud trial begins.
key_facts: Sam Bankman-Fried, age 31, is on trial for seven counts of fraud and conspiracy; the trial started on a Tuesday.
Bankman-Fried co-founded Alameda Research in 2017 and FTX in 2019 to bring revenue and liquidity to the trading arm.
In January 2022 FTX raised $400 million in a Series C round at a $32 billion valuation, its last round of public funding.
In 2021 FTX bought naming rights to the Miami Heat's home arena and partnered with celebrities such as Tom Brady, Gisele Bündchen, Steph Curry, Shaquille O'Neal and Naomi Osaka.
CoinDesk published Alameda's balance sheet showing $14.6 billion in assets and $8 billion in liabilities as of June 30, 2022.
Alameda held $5.82 billion in FTT tokens, 193% higher than the total FTT market cap of about $3 billion, meaning it purported to hold more FTT than existed.
Binance began pulling out its remaining $2.1 billion equivalent of BUSD and FTT, triggering a bank run on FTX.
FTX and Alameda filed for Chapter 11 in mid-November 2022; Bankman-Fried resigned and John J. Ray III became CEO.

Bankman-Fried was arrested in the Bahamas in December 2022 and released on a $250 million bail bond; house arrest at his parents' Palo Alto home was revoked in August after he was accused of intimidating Caroline Ellison by leaking her private diary.
Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison pleaded guilty in December 2022 and will cooperate with prosecutors as major witnesses.
Bankman-Fried pleaded not guilty in January and could face up to 115 years in jail if convicted on all charges.
John J. Ray III told a House committee that 'there were virtually no internal controls and no separateness whatsoever' at FTX.
Mark Cohen of Cohen & Gresser, who also represented Ghislaine Maxwell, is Bankman-Fried's lead attorney; his request for early release was denied.
BlockFi filed for Chapter 11 in November 2022 and Genesis Global Trading in January.
